device_name: Globus Creo Mcs Medial Cortical Screw Modular Pedicle Techniqueguide Reve

fields.what_it_is: CREO MCS® Midline Cortical Screw System. A comprehensive screw fixation platform available in preassembled and modular constructs. It provides enhanced cortical screw fixation paired with advanced interbody technology through a simple minimally invasive midline surgical approach. Modular screws enhance visibility at the operative site and access for decompression. Additional distraction of the disc space can be performed directly off of the screw posts, facilitating interbody spacer placement prior to rod insertion. The system features multiple options to fit varying patient anatomy. Preassembled and modular screws accept 5.5mm rods. CREO® modular screw shanks are also compatible with any CREO AMP® screw head and corresponding rods. Screws feature a Dual Outer Diameter (DOD) and cortical thread pitch to provide a better anatomical fit and enhanced fixation. Screws are designed based on morphometry and the cortical trajectory. The screws provide enhanced pullout strength compared to traditional screws. Polyaxial Screw: ±30° angulation (60° total) provides intraoperative versatility; Double lead thread for rapid insertion; 7mm DOD thread profile at the proximal end for enhanced cortical purchase and increased strength; Screw pitch designed to maintain cortical purchase; Drills and taps are color-coded to screw size. Screw Post: Double lead thread for rapid insertion; 7mm DOD thread profile at the proximal end for enhanced cortical purchase and increased strength; Screw pitch designed to maintain cortical purchase; Compatible with all CREO AMP® screw heads; Drills and taps are color-coded to screw size. Modular Screw Head: ±30° angulation (60° total) provides intraoperative versatility. Rods: 5.5mm diameter; Available in titanium alloy (TAV) and cobalt chrome (CoCr); Comprehensive selection of straight and curved rods: 35–150mm.

fields.compatible_with: CREO® modular screw shanks are also compatible with any CREO AMP® screw head and corresponding rods. Preassembled and modular screws accept 5.5mm rods. The system rods may be connected to the REVERE® Stabilization System (4.5mm, 5.5mm, or 6.35mm rod) or ELLIPSE® Occipito-Cervico-Thoracic Spinal System (3.5mm rod) using corresponding connectors. Refer to the corresponding CREO AMP® Technique Guide (GMTGD104 or GMTGD123). For a complete description of the ALTERA® technique, refer to the ALTERA® Technique Guide (GMTGD126).
fields.use_notes:
**Surgical Technique Steps:**
1. **Approach:** Patient placed prone and in flexion. Midline incision made over appropriate level(s). Use lateral C-arm fluoroscopy. Retract incision bilaterally, exposing spinous processes, pars interarticularis, and facet capsules. Dissection of pars and facets not required.
2. **Screw Trajectory:** Features a medial starting point (contrasts with lateral start of traditional pedicle screws). Cortical approach captures cortical areas of vertebral body. Avoid breaching lateral mass. Drilling and tapping of cortical bone required. Two-handed approach recommended during pedicle preparation.
3. **Site Preparation:** May require removal of excess soft tissue/bone. Use Pedicle Awl or high-speed burr to perforate pedicle cortex. Use Drill Guide with Adjustable Stop set to depth. Create pilot hole with appropriate drill, then reorient in final cortical trajectory. Drill slowly to prevent pars fractures. Use fluoroscopic guidance. Tap with appropriate sized Tap. Use Ball Tip Probe to ensure pedicle walls not violated.
4. **Screw Insertion:** Two options:
   - **Option A: Modular Screw:** Load screw post onto Modular Screwdriver. Drive screw posts into prepared pedicles. Distraction may be achieved using screw post heads with Parallel Head Distractor prior to screw head application. For screw head insertion: ensure clearance with Decortication Tool. Load screw head onto Head Inserter, lower onto screw post, apply axial force, then compress inserter handle to lock. Screw heads can be removed in situ using Head Release. All screw heads should be inserted and locked prior to rod insertion.
   - **Option B: Preassembled Screw:** Load screw onto Rigid Screwdriver. Drive screw into drilled/tapped holes.
5. **Rod Insertion and Locking Cap Delivery:** Determine rod length/contour using Rod Template. Rods may be contoured using Power Bender. Insert rod using Rod Holder. Two options for locking cap delivery:
   - **Option A: Locking Cap Driver, Short:** Load driver onto locking cap, insert into screw head, rotate 90° to capture rod. Can use Locking Cap Guide to aid adjustments.
   - **Option B: Semi-Automatic Locking Cap Driver:** Load up to eight caps, insert into screw head, rotate 90°, tilt driver along rod and lift to release cap. Only compatible with Reduction Fork for rod reduction.
6. **Rod Reduction:** Five options (max reduction): A. Locking Cap Guide (3mm), B. Reduction Fork (5mm), C. Geared Reducer, Pistol Grip (10mm), D. Geared Reducer, Overhead (10mm), E. Tower Reducer (20mm). Ensure rod properly contoured prior.
7. **Compression or Distraction:** Use Parallel Compressor or Parallel Distractor along rod. Tighten one set screw as rigid point. Provisionally tighten set screws after.
8. **Final Tightening:** Use Ratcheting Torque-Limiting Handle and Driver Shaft with Adjustable Counter-Torque. Final tighten set screws to torque limit (5.5Nm) and two audible clicks. Ensure done after corrective maneuvers.
**General Notes:** The Surgical Technique shown is for illustrative purposes only. The technique(s) actually employed always depends on the medical judgment of the surgeon. Instruments depicted may not be exactly the same as currently available; consult sales representative or Globus. Drilling and tapping of bone should be performed prior to decompression for best visualization. When placing screws, do not back out screws prior to finalizing the construct. Locking cap insertion requires minimal torque; if difficult, rod may not be seated properly. The construct is not completely locked until final tightening.
